Team — forwarding AcmeReady's redlines. High-level issue: they want full "defend and control" including AI-generated output (no carveout). Procurement deadline is tight.

My read: we should avoid open-ended defend-and-control for model output because of downstream risk and litigation control costs. Proposed internal compromise to draft for Acme:
1) Redwood will defend & control third-party IP claims that directly allege infringement by the Service (not downstream derivative uses) subject to: customer notice within 30 days of learning of claim, and Redwood's counsel leading litigation.
2) Exclude AI training-from-output claims unless customer provided the specific training dataset and expressly required training on that material.
3) Insurance offset: Redwood's insurance will be primary for covered claims up to policy limits; if claim falls outside policy, normal cap applies per order form.
4) Add mutual indemnity for customer breaches of customer-provided content (to avoid unilateral exposure).

I drafted a tracked version with targeted language; attaching supporting checklist. If we all agree, I’ll send a clean tracked_changes version back to Acme and propose a 30-minute call.

Thoughts?
KP

Hi Jane — thanks for the quick review and the annotated PDF. We appreciate AcmeReady’s concerns. Attached is a tracked draft (tracked_changes_indemnity.docx) with specific language intended to bridge our positions. High-level summary of the compromise:

- Defense & control: Redwood will assume defense and control for third-party IP claims that directly allege infringement by the Redwood Service as delivered (code, models, hosted inference), subject to prompt notice (30 days) and cooperation.
- AI-generated output: Excluded from automatic indemnity unless AcmeReady can show the claim relates to material Redwood was expressly directed to train on and which was marked as customer-supplied confidential training data. This protects us from broad downstream assertions about user-generated prompts/derivative outputs.
- Insurance/offsets: Redwood’s applicable insurance will be primary for covered IP claims up to policy limits. We have included a clause describing how offsets work in practice.
- Mutuality: Where claims arise from customer-supplied content or customer breach, AcmeReady will indemnify Redwood.
- Notice & control mechanics: 30-day notice window; if Acme fails to tender within 30 days Redwood may decline control; Redwood reserves the right to select counsel and to require settlement approval if settlement would materially affect Redwood’s operations.

We believe this is commercially reasonable and preserves both parties’ ability to manage litigation risk. If AcmeReady needs a faster cadence, we can hop on a 30-minute call — Ben and I are available 11/07 2:00–3:30pm PT.

If you’re amenable, we can push the tracked doc through DocuSign once you confirm.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
